newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer, PGMs also gain in price.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer, PGMs also gain in price.

text.p: Precious metals prices turned firmer on Tuesday afternoon spurred by fresh short covering by the investment funds and concerns over new delays in Russian platinum and palladium exports.
Dealers cited a possible stock market downturn following testimony later today by U.S. Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan before congress as a motivation to cover short positions.
Further the steadiness in gold of the past two days was both giving and receiving help from firmer platinum group metals, which were primarily supported by continuing delays in Russian exports.
Gold was fixed at $328.25 per ounce up $2.25 from the morning fix and $2.05 from Monday. The Comex August contract was $3.60 ahead at $329.80.
"Another try at $330.00 per ounce looks reasonably possible," a dealer said adding that a new price range of $322-$330 seemed to have been established.
Gold prices fell to their lowest level in 12 years earlier this month after the Reserve Bank of Australia announced it had sold 167 tonnes from reserves in the previous six months.
"We are still likely to see producers selling into any price rises and that will block progress," another dealer said.
Platinum and palladium were both firmer with most of the impetus coming from dealer covering in a tight market against rising doubts about Russian export patterns.

Russia, the second largest exporter of platinum and leading shipper of palladium, began the year's exports of palladium only a week ago and has yet to deliver any platinum to either the European dealer market or its leading customer Japan.
Platinum was indicated at $420.00/$423.00 up $8.50 and palladium was quoted at $200.00/$203.00, a gain of $11.50.
"Palladium seems to be available but platinum has notably taken second place in shipping to Japan," a market analyst said.

There were delays also in setting up contracts with dealers in Europe, he said. "Russia's European counterparties have been very slow to put prices in place. No shipments have arrived and only one company has done a deal," he said.
One snag was agreeing a forward price given that the market was so tight currently that cash prices were commanding a premium over prices for delivery dates later in the year.
"Changes in control have happened. The people involved may not be conversant with the ways of the market," the source said.
Silver was indicated at $4.34/$4.36 up seven cents.
